title: E-commerce orders
goal: Show the core entities and crow's-foot relationships of an e-commerce ordering domain.

rubric.must: Customer visibly has a one-to-many places relationship to Order.
Order visibly contains one or more line items and Product visibly relates to many line items.
Order visibly relates to payments and to a shipping address.
Customer, Order, Line Item, Product, Payment, and Address each appear as labelled entities with readable fields.
Primary-key and foreign-key fields are visibly marked in the entity tables.
Relationship endpoints visibly use crow's-foot cardinality notation.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the erd exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The drawing visibly shows all six entities, readable attributes and key markers, plus all six required crow’s-foot relationships with cardinalities consistent with the source.

items.evidence: CUSTOMER connects to ORDER through “places,” with exactly one at CUSTOMER and zero-or-many at ORDER.
ORDER “contains” one-or-many LINE_ITEM records; PRODUCT “appears_in” zero-or-many LINE_ITEM records.
ORDER connects to zero-or-many PAYMENT records through “has” and to exactly one ADDRESS through “ships_to”; an ADDRESS can serve zero-or-many orders.
CUSTOMER, ORDER, LINE_ITEM, PRODUCT, PAYMENT, and ADDRESS are all labelled and contain readable fields matching the source data.
Primary keys have visible blue PK badges and foreign keys have visible orange FK badges in the appropriate entity tables.
Relationship endpoints visibly use bars, circles, and crow’s feet to express exactly-one, zero-or-one, one-or-many, and zero-or-many cardinalities.
